question: Which of the following particles contribute to the mass number?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Protons and Neutrons**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **mass number** (represented by the symbol **A**) of an atom is defined as the total sum of the number of **protons** and **neutrons** present in its **nucleus**.
 
• **Protons** and **neutrons** are collectively known as **nucleons** because they reside within the atomic nucleus. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• The mass of an **electron** is approximately **1/1836** of the mass of a proton, which is considered **negligible** when calculating the overall mass number of an atom. ***Hence, statement 1 and 3 are incorrect.***
 
• While **protons** contribute to the mass, they are not the sole contributors; **neutrons** also provide nearly equal mass to the stability and weight of the nucleus. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• The mathematical formula for the mass number is **A = Z + N**, where **Z** is the **atomic number** (number of protons) and **N** is the **neutron number**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Atomic Number (Z):**

 
 
• This represents the total number of **protons** in the nucleus of an atom. It is unique to each **chemical element** and defines its position in the **Periodic Table**.
 
• In a neutral atom, the number of protons is equal to the number of **electrons**.
 
 
 
• **Isotopes:**
 
 
• These are atoms of the same element that have the same **atomic number** but different **mass numbers**.
 
• For example, **Hydrogen** has three isotopes: **Protium** (0 neutrons), **Deuterium** (1 neutron), and **Tritium** (2 neutrons).
 
 
 
• **Isobars:**
 
 
• These are atoms of different chemical elements that have the same **mass number** but different **atomic numbers**.
 
• An example includes **Argon-40** and **Calcium-40**.
 
 
 
• **Subatomic Particles Discovery:**
 
 
• **Electrons** were discovered by **J.J. Thomson** in **1897** using the cathode ray tube experiment.
 
• **Protons** were discovered by **Ernest Rutherford** in **1917** through his gold foil experiment.
 
• **Neutrons** were discovered by **James Chadwick** in **1932**, for which he was awarded the **Nobel Prize in Physics** in **1935**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mass of Particles:**

 
 
• The mass of a **proton** is approximately **1.00727 atomic mass units (amu)** or **1.6726 × 10^-27 kg**.
 
• The mass of a **neutron** is slightly higher, approximately **1.00866 amu** or **1.6749 × 10^-27 kg**.
 
• The mass of an **electron** is **0.000548 amu** or **9.1093 × 10^-31 kg**.
 
 
 
• **Nuclear Force:**
 
 
• The **protons** and **neutrons** are held together in the nucleus by the **strong nuclear force**, which is the strongest of the four fundamental forces of nature but acts over a very short range (about **1 femtometer**).
 
 
 
• **Representation:**
 
 
• An element is often represented as **AZX**, where **X** is the chemical symbol, **A** is the **mass number** (top), and **Z** is the **atomic number** (bottom).
